extracted.intended_audience: general readers and practitioners interested in 18th-century Mediterranean travel, agriculture, and food-production techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive travel narrative documenting landscapes, agricultural practices, climates, prices, and local technologies; useful as a model or source of practical agricultural and preservation techniques observed in situ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packing bottled wine
rubrics_metrics.description: The best method of packing wine, when bottled, is to lay the bottles on their side, and cover them with sand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: advice given alongside cellar details (e.g., cellar temperature 9.5° Reaumur) and specifications of large casks/tons; intended to reduce breakage and preserve bottles during storage/transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving fresh figs
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve figs: dry them in the sun without putting anything to them whatever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variants and market notes: Marseilles figs ('figues Marseilloises') keep long when dried; prices vary (e.g., 15 sous/pound for best). Fresh figs exude sugar in spring and become sour if not dried.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving raisins (grapes)
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve raisins: first dip the grape in ley, then dry it in the sun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to certain dried grapes (e.g., Smyrna raisins). Method described as the process used locally for raisin preservation prior to sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caper cultivation and harvest routine
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant capers in quincunx about eight feet apart; cover plants in winter with a foot-high earthen hill; each plant must be picked every day as the fruit forms on the extending stem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labor and yield: gathering is done by women (can gather ~12 pounds/day); a bush yields ~2 pounds/year valued at about twelve sous/pound; plants are long-lived and will grow even in walls or poor soil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Olive-tree economics and lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolerably good olive trees yield about twenty pounds of oil per tree; an olive tree must be about twenty years old before it has paid its own expenses; trees last for very long periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market and risk notes: oil prices vary (e.g., 10–16 sous/pound depending on quality/virgin status); olive grounds and lease rates cited; extreme cold events can devastate crops but old roots may sprout again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vine training with forked-staff arbors
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant clusters of vines at intervals (~8 feet); at each cluster fix a forked staff with a horizontal cross-piece about eight feet from the ground, creating an arbor eight feet wide and high; train vines over successive cross-pieces to form long covered arbors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical description of a local arbor system: clusters of 2–6 plants per stake, vines brought up the fork and laid over the crosspieces to form continuous shaded arbors for the row.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vine training using poles between trees
rubrics_metrics.description: Lash poles from tree to tree along rows, set vines between trees and train them over the pole so that alternating intervals form arbors and open spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative local method to create shade/arbors by integrating vines with existing orchard/tree rows; noted as another observed regional technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willow quick-set hedges
rubrics_metrics.description: Form quick-set hedges by planting willows from one to three feet apart; when grown 8–10 feet high, bend them down and interlace them with each other to create a living hedge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation: this practice is used but many such hedges do not seem to become old (may have limited longevity); useful for delineation and windbreaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rice paddy cultivation sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: To sow rice: plough the ground, level it with a drag-harrow, let on water, smooth the surface with a shovel while under water, and then sow the rice in the water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Water management: keep fields under shallow water after sowing, draw off after six weeks or two months to weed, then re-flood until August and draw off a few weeks before harvest (September). Rice yields and labor economy: same measure of ground yields ~3× wheat with half the labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rice-beating and processing workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a multi-pestle rice-beating machine driven by a water-wheel: arms lift and drop pestles into mortars; after beating, rice is sifted multiple times through suspended sifters and returned to mortars until finished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machine specs and throughput: pestles e.g., 5.25 inches square, 10 ft long, conical iron-covered ends; timing examples: six pestles clear ~4000 pounds in 24 hours; detailed sifting sequence and durations provided; alternative tooth-armed pestles described for faster cleaning and less breakage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design details for rice-pestles and beaters
rubrics_metrics.description: Pestles have specified dimensions and forms (e.g., length ~10 ft, square section, truncated-cone iron-covered end or teeth-armed cones); arranged ~10.5 inches apart and driven to give multiple strokes per wheel revolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineering notes: two arms per pestle to give two strokes per revolution; mortars under pestles sized to allow vertical motion; variations (stone mortars vs. wood) and claimed benefits (durability, cleaning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grape drying siting and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Best grapes for drying (raisins) are grown against a southern wall to provide sufficient sun to dry the abundant juice; drying in sun is principal preservation method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Varietal notes: 'des Panses' described as best for drying (large, thick skin, much juice); drying practices influence market value and storage life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cheese and butter production steps and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: For butter: milk is scummed, cream separated and churned in a cylindrical churn (dimensions given) with three inward staves and an iron axis, turned ~1.5 hours by two men; for cheese: milk processing includes scumming and using remaining milk for cheese with described handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational details: example herd sizes and milk yields (e.g., 85 cows, ten cows yield a brenta of milk in two milkings), timing for scumming, churn dimensions (radius 18 in, thickness 14 in), and connections between butter and cheese making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale/order of plant hardiness by altitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed gradation of tender plants ascending/descending mountains: caper, orange, palm, aloe, olive, pomegranate, walnut, fig, almond (from most tender to hardiest among listed plants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use: practical guide for what species will survive at given elevations and exposures; author notes this is for plants themselves and that fruiting order can differ. Observations based on ascending/descending several passes through mountainous zones.
